purpose: precision and recall of extracted (character, direction) claims at comment level (plan 5.3, scored by aimediator.measurement.score_positions)
labels_without_model_outputs: Labels were written by the annotation session U0-A from the text_original of each comment only. The session read no claims, quarantined claims, audit results, relevance decisions, requests or responses of the archived run. From the run it read extraction-coverage.json only to select the IDs (comment_id, claims_generated, disposition); the selection group is not recorded per comment, and comments were labeled in the set order without it.
selection: From the 525 entries of extraction-coverage.json (one per comment): every comment with claims_generated above 0 (251), plus the first 50 comments, ordered by the hexadecimal SHA-256 of the UTF-8 string "extraction-precision-v1:<record_id>" ascending, with claims_generated 0 and a disposition other than generation_failed (272 eligible). The text of each comment is the text_original of its source dataset row, checked against content_sha256.
split: development when int(first 8 hexadecimal digits of SHA-256 of "extraction-precision-v1:<record_id>", base 16) modulo 10 is below 7, or when the record_id is in latency-benchmark-v1 (27 of its 60 IDs are in this set; 8 of them are forced into development); test otherwise.
test_split_policy: The test split runs once, in U7.2; no session tunes against it (plan rule 1.11).
order: labels.jsonl lists the comments by the hexadecimal SHA-256 of "extraction-precision-v1:<record_id>", ascending.

fields.positions: every (character, direction) position the author takes, as objects with character and direction
fields.exhaustive: true: positions lists every position of the comment, so an unlisted character or direction is not a position
fields.uncertain: true when the author's position cannot be resolved; score_positions excludes these comments from precision and recall and counts them apart
fields.reason: one or two English sentences, quoting the source where needed

label_policy.position: A fighter whose balance the author takes a stance on. A mention, a comparison, a victim, the author's own character, roster wishes, story, cosmetic design or praise is not a position. System-only feedback (Drive, throw loops, modern controls, netcode, monetization) gives positions [] with that reason.
label_policy.directions: buff: the author wants the fighter stronger, calls it too weak, or objects to its nerfs; nerf: wants it weaker, calls it too strong or cheap, or objects to its buffs; keep: a clear request to preserve, or approval of, its balance; unclear: a balance stance whose requested change cannot be established (meanings of the extraction prompt). One comment may hold two directions for one fighter when it asks for both.
label_policy.characters: Glossary canonical names (src/aimediator/assets/data/glossary.json), including the glossary aliases and labels and plain transliteration variants of a canonical name (for example 吉米 for Jamie, 雅思敏 for Yasmine, 阿利克斯 for Alex); a move name scoped to one character in the glossary identifies that character. A name outside the glossary keeps its source literal and is flagged in reason; a nationality-only nickname never establishes identity.
label_policy.source_literals_note: source_literals counts the positions of every comment, uncertain ones included. The literals 阿俊 and Arjun probably name the same character (Arjun, listed in the glossary roster_policy as a future character and absent from the glossary entries); they are kept apart as source literals. A scorer that maps both to one name changes the comparison and must say so.
label_policy.uncertain: Set when a stance cannot be resolved: sarcasm the text itself does not settle, a character named only by nationality or by an unresolvable nickname, or a statement that may not be a balance stance. Positions that can be resolved are still listed. A request with no textual cue of sarcasm is labeled literally.

created: 2026-11-04 (pipeline upgrade step U0.5, annotation session U0-A)
